items.note: S2.4.1 reproduces Lemma lem:scalar-motifs faithfully (eight-row copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule, y_S+x_S for arbitrary scratch, three stages giving (-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored). Nothing derives it: the net change (JV+RG)x and the central coefficients |S cap T| mod 2 or (|S cap T|-1)/2 are only alluded to in S2.4.3.1, and h=100, the neighbour rules and the wire counts are absent.

The sub-steps follow the paper's invariant argument (common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, intermediate frames free to make edges cheap). The route operator omits the scalar sign epsilon_w (lines 818-822), which matters for the complex bank exchange, and the headline of S2.4.2 drops S_Omega.

Lemma lem:motif-residuals (comparable labels, only central 3->4 edges decreasing by h, L=Ich, sum |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L) and the ratios 100/539, 101/539 are stated exactly. The derivation stops at the triple pairing: the stage labels A,B,P,Q, the gate-label table eq:motif-labels, the residual table and the telescoping (sources sum to N, sinks to Wm-N) behind Wm-2N+2L are missing, as are the F_2 dot product and the orthonormal-basis clause.

The rank-sum half follows the proof: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, plus the N rank-one first edges 2P_{U_a} of the negative source projections, giving s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0. The endpoint identity I_m is only asserted. Its check (P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m, with zero source and identity sink on the other roles) and the shear frames Phi_M that turn it into H<-H+D are absent.

S2.4.3.5 gives one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector and s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m. It omits 'or its inverse' (line 1218), does not define the phase frames C_U, and does not state that after diagonal corrections every role receives C^{tensor m}; S2.6.1 only implies the last point. No derivation (weight additivity mod 4, the Z_a corrections) is given.

L/N<1/2, s_b<W_b m, s_c<W_c m, and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} from deficits above 20*2^{-50} and log m<20 are all stated correctly. S2.4.4 is an inference: the exact eta values and the inequality m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta) are not worked out.

S2.2 lists the four elementary operations correctly. S2.3 gives the controlled shift with its split-and-merge mechanism, but its claim drops the hypothesis that the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time (line 566), and it omits multiplication by fixed rational units.

The shear-cost route matches lines 1425-1446: lower-triangular factors are done as controlled shifts in tape order, and each one of Pi costs D_j<-D_j+H_i, one swap, then D_j<-H_i-D_j. The elimination proof of A=E_1 Pi E_2 is only quoted, and the claim omits the fixed odd prime q and the arithmetic over Z/q^b.

These steps follow the proof: cyclic row split into W streams, only the middle of three shears through the network, s calls on V/W, an O(V) depth-first schedule, then the recurrence and the two-case geometric sum. The Phi_M frame step is implicit through S2.4.2 and S2.4.3.4. The statement gives F_k=O(e^tau) but not the proposition's hypotheses (chunks of e=m^k radix-q digits, row field divisible by W^k) or the O(Ve^tau) interchange itself.

The plan follows the proof: the top rho digits are exchanged and joined into a row field at cost O(V rho), then padded to a multiple of W^k; the remaining width is expanded in base m into power-width calls costing O(Ve^tau); and [2^u] is padded to [q^e] with e=O(u).

Two steps are missing: that P_M is a fixed number of row additions by Gaussian elimination (lines 1892-1901, the link to the packed procedure), and the Z_{a,f} and i^{27f} endpoint corrections that give C^{tensor e} on every role (lines 1907-1913).

The time bound, the eight parity operations, the bad set with |B|<=delta_bad M, and the radix-sort repair are all present. The argument that T_0 S_0^{-1} fixes B^c and permutes only B (lines 2107-2114), which is what makes the sorted reinsertion correct, is missing. So are the separate XOR at j_{f-1} and how each rotation is done (chunk swap plus controlled shift, the source of L^tau).

S1 alludes to the n log n order through Schonhage-Strassen and Harvey-van der Hoeven. No step states the eventual lower bound, its liminf negation, or that the theorem refutes the conjecture in this model.

errors.says: the O(n log n) bound means 'a further saving must beat a logarithmic factor by a power'
errors.paper: The paper only says it obtains a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor. It does not claim that any further improvement must be a power saving.

errors.says: the exchange network has 'W wires of rank-m labels'
errors.paper: Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional space F^{tensor 3}, with dimensions from 0 (scratch sources) to m. Only the ambient space, and so the per-wire budget, has dimension m.

errors.says: the array network applies only the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1} to each role (and S2.4.2.2 gives the route operator as D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1})
errors.paper: The implemented operator is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and a route applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} with its scalar sign. In the complex network the sign -1 must later be removed by negating outputs.

errors.says: indicator vectors satisfy <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1, so triple lines are nondegenerate and neighbouring lines orthogonal
errors.paper: That pairing is the rational form x^T(I-J/9)y of the bit network, with self-pairing 2. The complex network's labels use F_2^h with the dot product (t_T.t_T=1), where neighbours have even intersection.

errors.says: each phase-frame difference is a product of one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector
errors.paper: Each factor is the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse; the sign is negated on decreasing edges.

errors.says: a controlled update y -> y+a(controls) mod Q of a later field costs O(V)
errors.paper: This holds provided the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time from the controls, each having O(b) digits.

errors.says: 'The remaining records are extracted, given their destination ranks, sorted ... and reinserted'
errors.paper: Only the exceptional records in B are extracted and sorted. This works because T_0 S_0^{-1} fixes the complement of B and permutes B.

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. It goes from the scalar bank-exchange network, frames, subspace labels and the rank budget s<Wm to tau=1-2^{-50}, then to the interchange recursion and the phase-frame layer recursion. From there it passes through synthetic transforms and retained-order convolution, resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation, CRT, twist and assembly, to exact recovery and the cost table with minimum margin 2 kappa. It thins out where it quotes instead of deriving: the label construction and the telescoping behind Wm-2N+2L, the endpoint identity and its shear frames Phi_M, the one-dimensional Gaussian resampling identity, the guard-width and source-error (E_s) chains, and the setup and exceptional-stream accounting in the final bound.

steps.note: The fixed linear network with the eight-row schedule, the exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and every scratch wire restored is stated explicitly, and triples index the data. The plan never gives h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 or m=h^3; N and m appear only as symbols.

These steps carry the common frame commuting with a pointwise gate, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and edges paying only D_vD_u^{-1}, with intermediate frames chosen to be cheap. The route sign epsilon_w is omitted.

Nested nondegenerate subspaces of F^{tensor 3} from triple indicator vectors, every edge joining comparable labels, and only the central 3->4 edges decreasing, each by h, are all stated. 'Dimension m' appears only loosely, as 'rank-m labels'.
S2.4.3.4.1 states rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, unchanged on reversal. S2.4.3.4.2 adds the N negative source projections whose first edge has rank one with no dimension change.
L=Ich, sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b are stated. The telescoping that produces the budget (sources N, sinks Wm-N) is not shown.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 are both below 1/2, giving deficit N-2L_b>0 and s<Wm for both networks.

S2.4.3.4 states that the endpoint matrices differ by I_m on every input role, and S2.4.6.2 that the network performs the middle shear H<-H+D. The step connecting them, matrices used as shear frames Phi_M so that the endpoints give Phi_{I_m}, is implicit and its proof (P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m) is absent.

A=E_1 Pi E_2 with lower-triangular factors, the triangular work as linear controlled shifts, one interchange per one of Pi (exactly a interchanges plus O(V)), and exactly s recursive calls per node are all present.

These carry children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), tau=1-2^{-50} from deficits above 20*2^{-50} and log m<20, and the two-case geometric sum giving F_k=O(e^tau). The exact eta values are not given.

central.summary: The S2.4 subtree carries all nine steps of the central saving in the paper's order: fixed exchange network, frames, labels, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget, L/N<1/2 so s<Wm, the endpoint identity, edges as rank-many recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The weaker points are that h=100, N and m are never given numerically, that the budget and the endpoint identity are asserted rather than derived, and that the passage from I_m to the shear H<-H+D through Phi_M frames is left implicit.
